answer.rationale: The binding constraint is delivery risk: the line is at 94% with no buffer and the only primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renewal, so the single action this cycle must secure continuity. A primary switch or a new source in that window is a forced cutover and would raise stop-the-line risk even if memory_c2’s prior onboarding was ‘quick’; TCO includes that disruption, which would swamp an 18% piece-price save. Mid-cycle the incumbent already refused to reopen price, so spending the only decision on negotiate_terms or defer_decision risks a supply cliff if talks fail or month-to-month does not appear. Renewing the incumbent follows memory_c1 (stable integration, no migration, deliveries held) and does not increase delivery risk. memory_c2 is the highest-VOI check on whether switch risk is actually negligible; until that archive is seen, uncertainty on transition risk is preserved and the low-cost quote is not treated as a free lunch.
